summary.name: Prism
summary.one_liner: Prism is an open-source download manager that splits files into parallel connections, captures browser downloads, and saves videos, for Windows, macOS, and Linux.
use_cases: capture downloads started in a browser
download HLS or DASH video streams
summary.what_it_does: Prism splits each file into segments and runs up to 32 connections per file, reassigning connections to the largest remaining range when one finishes. It writes directly into the final file rather than assembling a copy at the end. Resume is crash-safe: data is flushed to disk before progress is saved, and ETag or Last-Modified is checked on resume. It supports HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, FTP/FTPS, HLS and DASH streams, and the page describes browser capture, video downloads, queues and a scheduler. The page also includes a speed table by file-size range, with example average speeds from 962 KB/s to 1.9 MB/s.
notable: Up to 32 parallel connections per file with per-host memory and back-off for servers that limit connections
Writes directly into the final file with no assembly copy at the end
Crash-safe resume validated with ETag / Last-Modified
Supports HLS and DASH streams alongside HTTP and FTP
caveats: Speed figures in the table are example measurements on the page and may vary by server and network
Listed as freeware in awesome-mac; the page itself does not state a license or price beyond open source
